parentReview.reason: Candidate contradicts Beta 1.7.3 scope: includes Beta 1.8 content (melon, rotten flesh, enderman, silverfish, blocks 97-109 and items 360-368), omits wool block 35, and conflates wool metadata with dye item metadata. Artifact hash alone does not validate the extraction/classpath provenance.
parentReview.requiredNextStep: Re-extract registries from a hash-verified b1.7.3 jar with executable provenance-bound tooling and introduction-version negative controls. Independently verify wool and dye mappings. No entry in this candidate is approved for gameplay enforcement.

generatedNote: Derived from official Mojang jars only (b1.7.3 client, 26.3 vanilla). No wiki, no third-party list, no runtime execution.

scope.objective: Strict server-side acquisition allowlist source for a Beta 1.7.3 profile on Minecraft 26.3.
inScope: block/item/entity registry identity and numeric ids in b1.7.3
scope.enforcement: Parent architecture decides enforcement. Unknown mappings fail closed: nothing in this file is to be treated as allowed unless obtainable=true and mappingConfidence=high.

b173.verification: sha1 equals launchermeta version_manifest_v2 -> b1.7.3.json downloads.client.sha1 (verified in-session)
b173.extraction: registration sites read from class shapes. Proven: Block.<init>(int id, Material) assigns blocks[id]; Item.<init>(int arg) assigns items[256+arg]; Block.<clinit> then fills item slots for blocks 0..255 with new ItemBlock(id-256).
b173.entityExtraction: EntityList.addMapping(Class, String, int) - all 28 registrations read from the jar.

mc263.verificationLevel: declaration-level. Registry ids are derived from static final field names in Blocks/Items/EntityTypes (field name lowercased equals registry path) plus the ColorCollection-backed colour families. NO 26.3 process was executed, so 'exists in the 26.3 registry' is sourced from the shipped class files, not from a running server.

metadataRemapWarnings.warning: b1.7.3 metadata order for wool/dye is NOT the 26.3 DyeColor ordinal order; the legacy order is black-first and the modern ordinal order is white-first. Any port must remap by these lists, not by ordinal.
metadataRemapWarnings.slugException: legacy metadata 7 is 'silver' which is 26.3 light_gray; legacy metadata 12 is 'lightBlue' which is 26.3 light_blue.
metadataRemapWarnings.slabNote: b1.7.3 STEP metadata 0..3 only; the brick and smooth-stone-brick slabs were added in 1.8.
metadataRemapWarnings.bedNote: b1.7.3 beds are red only; metadata 0 and 8 both mean red. Modern white_bed and every other colour must not be allowlisted for 1.7.3.

inputs.name: Minecraft b1.7.3 client jar
inputs.verified: SHA-1 recomputed locally equals downloads.client.sha1 in version_manifest_v2 -> b1.7.3.json
inputs.usedFor: legacy registry identity, numeric ids, metadata variant tables, entity network ids

method.legacyBlocks: Registration sites read from the Block class: Block.<init>(int id, Material) stores blocks[id]; the legacy name comes from the .a("<name>") call on the same constructor chain. Each id is paired with its name at the registration line, so the pairing is positional and unambiguous.
method.legacyItems: Item.<init>(int arg) stores items[256 + arg] and sets the item's numeric id to 256 + arg. Item ids in this file are therefore 256 + constructor arg, NOT the raw constructor argument. This is why bucket (arg 69) is id 325 and milk (arg 79) is id 335.
method.legacyBlockItems: Block.<clinit> fills item slots for blocks 0..255 with new ItemBlock(id - 256), so a block's item id equals its block id for ids below 256.
method.legacyEntities: EntityList registrations (class, name, networkId). The networkId is a wire id, not a registry index.
method.modernBlocksAndItems: Static final field names in net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks and net.minecraft.world.item.Items; the field name lowercased is the registry path.
method.modernColourFamilies: Families stored as ColorCollection records (bed, wool, dye, banner, carpet, concrete, ...) are not individual fields; their ids are <colour>_<suffix>. They were expanded from the ColorCollection field list plus the 16 colours.
method.modernEntities: Static final field names in net.minecraft.world.entity.EntityTypes; EntityTypeIds holds the matching ResourceKeys.
method.tools: javap (JDK 25) on the shipped class files, and constant-pool/field scanning. No game process was executed; no wiki or third-party list was used.

confidenceModel.high: identity is unambiguous: unique legacy name with an established modern equivalent, or a documented rename.
confidenceModel.medium: identity is plausible but a historical choice remains open (which modern wood variant represents a single-wood-type legacy block; one modern fish species standing in for a single legacy fish; the giant mob; boats).
confidenceModel.low: identity not established at all (block id 97). Fails closed.

knownExpectedDuplicates.note: Several legacy blocks legitimately map to the same modern id (fluid, metadata-merged, lit/unlit variants). Duplicates are therefore not errors; they are listed so a consumer can see them explicitly.
modernIdsReusedByMoreThanOneLegacyBlock: brown_mushroom (id 39 block, id 99 mushroom block shape)
red_mushroom (id 40 block, id 100 mushroom block shape)
wood-backed ids shared by pressurePlate pairs and stem pairs

reproduce: 1. Download the b1.7.3 client jar and confirm SHA-1 43db9b498cb67058d2e12d394e6507722e71bb45.

2. Decompile or disassemble the obfuscated root classes; locate the class whose constructor assigns itself into a 256-entry array (the Block class, id 'lr' in this jar) and the class that assigns into a 32000-entry array at 256+arg (the Item class, 'sv').
3. Read the Block field declarations and the Block static initialiser for the (id, name) pairs.
4. Read the Item field declarations for (constructor arg, name) and add 256.
5. Read EntityList registrations for the entity list.
6. Read the 26.3 jar's Blocks/Items/EntityTypes field names, expand ColorCollection families, then map by name.
